errors: "39 of the 41 migrations ... took under 5 seconds" is not established; the facts say most did.
"Pod 1 re-acquires the lock" and "the 180-second cycle repeats" add an exact retry sequence not verified in the incident facts.
"the 4m10s migration can never finish" overstates the evidence and does not explain how the outage ended.
"The Job ... has no liveness probe" is an unverified configuration presented as fact.
"runs it to completion" and "pods start immediately" promise outcomes beyond removing the migration from pod startup.
"a deploy pipeline Job does not" kill a long-running migration ignores unverified Job timeout and termination settings.
R01.note: It explains the observed outage clearly, but repeats itself and turns a proposed Job configuration into guaranteed completion.

errors: "39 of the last 41 migrations took under 5 seconds" is not established.
"The Job has its own timeout" asserts configuration that has not been checked.
"it can't take the API down" ignores schema incompatibility and database blocking during migration.
"roughly one migration in 20 is a risk" treats migrations over 120 seconds as evidence of exceeding the 180-second restart threshold.
"I'd then do the Job the next time a migration comes close to the limit" assumes a warning opportunity that the evidence does not establish.
R02.note: The alternative and its recovery tradeoff are useful, but the answer understates compatibility risks and exaggerates what the migration statistics establish.

errors: "39 of 41 migrations were under 5s" is not established.
"runs once to completion with no probes to kill it" assumes an unverified Job configuration and guarantees completion.
R03.note: It gives a compact causal explanation of the benefit, but supplies neither the supporting configuration nor the conditions needed for the Job to deliver it.

errors: "That has happened once" asserts an incident count when only one incident is supplied.
"At 180s, the liveness probe started failing" confuses the restart threshold with the start of probe failures.
"Every migration is fine until one runs long, and then it takes the API down" generalizes one observed outage to every long migration.
"compatible with the old code ... is true of an index build" assumes adding an index cannot disrupt service through locking or other effects.
"A Job is the only option here where that limit doesn't apply" overlooks a startup probe that can defer liveness checks.
R04.note: It usefully identifies compatibility and timeout checks as unfinished, but several absolute claims contradict that otherwise careful uncertainty.

errors: "39 of 41 migrations took under 5 seconds" is not established.
"This only happens ... and for the 2 slow ones it did" incorrectly treats both migrations over two minutes as exceeding the three-minute liveness limit.
"The Job ... has no readiness or liveness check" presents an unverified configuration as fact.
"a 4-minute index build finishes" guarantees completion beyond the evidence.
"Nothing restarts them" and "the old pods keep serving orders" are unconditional promises despite unverified compatibility and database blocking.
"each slower index build needs the limit raised again" assumes each subsequent build exceeds the newly configured allowance.
"Two of the last 41 did" incorrectly claims both slow migrations exceeded 180 seconds.
R05.note: The compatibility and database-locking caveats help decision-making, but the answer repeatedly confuses the two-minute statistic with the three-minute kill threshold.

errors: "existing API pods keep serving" is not guaranteed by schema compatibility alone; migration locking and Job configuration remain unverified.
"the two slow index builds" implies both benefited from avoiding the liveness threshold, although only one is established to have exceeded 180 seconds.
R06.note: It explains the benefit economically and acknowledges schema compatibility, but leaves the configuration supporting the argument unseen.

errors: "a failed migration stops it" describes intended pipeline gating without explicitly distinguishing it from verified existing behavior.
"existing pods keep serving" remains conditional on database effects as well as the acknowledged schema compatibility requirement.
R07.note: It gives the strongest evidence-calibrated explanation and admits the missing source excerpts, although that admission does not replace showing the configuration.

errors: "all three pods wait on one Postgres advisory lock" misstates the supplied sequence: one holds the lock and two wait.
"Deploy starts 3 new pods" assumes an unverified rollout sequence.
"are killed again" adds a repeated-kill sequence not explicitly verified.
"This happens only when a migration outlasts" excludes lock waiting and other causes of exceeding the startup allowance.
"the Job finishing once" and "new pods then starting at once" guarantee completion and immediate startup.
"there is no observable difference: pods wait a few seconds either way" contradicts moving the migration wait out of the pods.
R08.note: It makes the mechanism understandable, but repeatedly restates it and presents illustrative commands without actual source locations.

errors: "39 of the 41 migrations" under five seconds is not established.
"The benefit shows up on the other 2" assumes both exceeded the 180-second limit.
"./server" invents an entrypoint command.
"livenessProbe: {}" is not verified source and does not encode the claimed 180-second threshold.
"orders requests stop being routed" precisely at 120 seconds assumes unverified routing and rollout details.
"the half-applied migration is whatever Postgres rolled back to" assumes unverified transaction and rollback behavior.
"starts the index build again — from the start" is not established.
"The loop only ends when ... finishes inside a 180s window" invents how the incident recovered.
"The Job has no liveness probe" asserts unverified configuration.
"their prisma migrate deploy sees nothing to do" retains an entrypoint migration command despite the proposed move out of that entrypoint.
"orders stay up" is unsupported without compatibility and database-locking checks.
"that is the whole cost" omits compatibility requirements, failure handling, and Job configuration.
R09.note: Its apparent precision comes from invented code and recovery mechanics, making the long explanation less trustworthy than the supplied facts.

errors: "39 of 41 migrations ... under 5 seconds" is not established.
"got killed again" adds a repeated-kill sequence not explicitly verified.
"No amount of tuning the probes fixes this cleanly" dismisses alternatives with a verdict and overlooks startup-probe options.
"can take 4 minutes without anything killing it" overstates removing a liveness probe.
"half-applied schema" asserts an unverified database state.
"costs one Job manifest plus a pipeline step" omits removing entrypoint migration execution and checking compatibility.
R10.note: It identifies the relevant timing conflict but substitutes jargon and absolutes for the configuration and asks again about work already requested.

errors: "any pod that isn't healthy within 3 minutes" generalizes the orders service's configured probe behavior to any pod.
"hits the 3-minute limit again" adds a repeated-kill sequence not explicitly verified.
"safely take as long as it needs" ignores Job termination settings and migration effects on the database.
"existing pods will stay up and serve traffic normally" assumes unverified schema compatibility and absence of database blocking.
R11.note: The startup-to-restart sequence is easy to follow, but the promised uninterrupted service exceeds the evidence.

errors: "39 of 41 migrations took under 5 seconds" is not established.
"fine until a migration builds an index, and then it takes the whole API down" falsely treats every index build as an outage trigger.
"Nothing kills it partway through" ignores unverified Job timeout and termination settings.
"The old pods keep serving" assumes compatibility and absence of database blocking.
"Today a failed migration means pods crash and restart in a loop" generalizes beyond the verified slow-migration incident.
"Adding a column or an index is fine" guarantees safety without examining the operation or running code.
"Renaming or dropping a column needs two deploys" asserts a universal deployment count without knowing the migration strategy.
"will probably break the current setup" predicts failure from the presence of an index alone.
"the Canva and claude.ai Todoist connectors need authorization" introduces entirely unsupported and unrelated connector claims.
R12.note: It explains the observed failure but turns index builds into predicted outages and ends with unrelated, invented connector requirements.
